title: Separate reserved-capacity credit attribution for multi-region tenants to prevent negative invoice lines
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers with Dedicated capacity spanning multiple cloud regions are receiving invoices with either negative line items or duplicate reserved-capacity credits. Root cause appears to be the current billing export consolidating all reserved-capacity discounts into a single tenant-level credit line during the Stripe -> Netsuite export. When a tenant has usage and reserved pools located in different regions (and therefore different plan IDs / pricing dimensions), the single consolidated credit is applied to the most recent invoice bucket and sometimes gets proration applied incorrectly, producing negative line items or double-counted credits in mid-cycle adjustments.

Goal: Make reserved-capacity credits region-aware in exports and reconcile historical invoices where consolidation caused inaccuracies. Approach: 1) change export generator to unbundle reserved-capacity credits into region-scoped export lines (include region tag and reserved_pool_id); 2) compute prorated credit per region using the same hour-level anchoring as usage lines; 3) ensure export line fingerprints contain reserved_pool_id+region to make them idempotent; 4) add detection and repair runner to backfill affected invoices and write repair events to audit logs.

Trade-offs considered: a) Keep single consolidated credit (less export volume) vs unbundling (more stable, maps cleanly to Netsuite segments). We chose unbundling because it reduces ambiguity during downstream invoice reconciliation and ties credits to the resource causing the discount. b) Apply backfill automatically vs require manual review. We will auto-generate repair candidates but gate automatic invoice adjustments behind a configurable threshold and human approval for customer-visible negative-line changes.

Success criteria: 1) zero new cases of negative invoice line creation for multi-region tenants in staging; 2) export fingerprints unique per region and reserved_pool_id; 3) backfill runner closes > 95% of historical bad invoices without manual edits in the repair window; 4) downstream Netsuite reconciliation shows a stable export signature for affected invoices.

Rollout plan: feature-flag export unbundle in staging -> run shadow export against current export for one week -> compare diffs using shadow-compare harness -> enable in prod for non-critical tenants -> run backfill repair for accumulated discrepancy set in batches with manual approval for > $500 adjustments.

Artifacts: Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/BILL/Region-aware+Reserved+Capacity+Credit+Unbundling; Shadow export diff dashboard: https://analytics.redwood.ai/d/exports/shadow-diff; Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/5823
